utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall now turn to Mr. Mundis to hear from him about the schedule for the days to come. According to the understanding of the Chamber, we have two witnesses on standby. One, as I have said, could appear on the 12th and the 13th of July. For the other one, I don't know. So could you give us some additional information, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The last contact that we had with the other witness was Friday of last week, at which point the witness informed us that he would be unable to travel for approximately 15 days. In light of what the Trial Chamber has informed us earlier today about the availability of a witness for the 12th and 13th, it seems to us that the 13th and/or 14th would be the best appropriate time to bring the remaining witness, assuming that he is in fact able to travel by then. That would be outside the 15-day window. We will endeavour this afternoon to contact that witness, and if he is available in that time period, we will ensure that VWS brings that witness in for that time period. If that's successful, we would then be in a position to have completed the hearings with respect to the witnesses by the 14th of July, and of course, as we've said before, hopefully by then we can have the documents resolved and we would then be in a position to close our case. As I said, we will endeavour to bring the second witness here so that he is able to testify perhaps on the 13th if the first witness is done, or on the 14th. I anticipate the second witness will be very, very brief in light of the fact that he's a crime-base witness and his testimony shouldn't take more than, in total, a couple of hours. If that's acceptable, we'll certainly endeavour to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. The Chamber will by that date certainly render its written decision regarding documents, and then either the 14th or the 15th of July you could then close your case, and then we will enter the stage which is 98 bis, as we mentioned yesterday. We will discuss amongst ourselves again whether the three weeks are fully justified, and then again the Prosecution would have three weeks to respond, so this will bring us to the beginning of September. So everything depends on these two witnesses, that is, when exactly they will come. Has the Defence any observations to make at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you Mr. President. Your Honours, I would simply like to return to the question of documents that were used by the Chamber when asking questions of witnesses on Monday. They are contested documents 585 and 586. These are documents which possibly come from the court of Zenica and the court of Travnik. These are documents which the Defence jointly objected to regarding the admissibility of documents because we don't know exactly how and where the Prosecution obtained these documents nor what exactly those documents represent, how they were used and by whom, and our main objection is that we need a witness to add to the reliability of these documents so that they may be of use to the Chamber. A witness was identified who should come before the Chamber to do this, that is, for these particular documents. And we had a witness quite recently, a judge from the Zenica court, who could have easily been able to confirm or reject the purpose of these documents. However, the Prosecution did not use him for that purpose. We also wish to say that we still haven't received a translation in one of the official languages of the Tribunal of these documents. Finally, the Defence wishes to say that the Defence maintains its objection to documents 585, 586, which we received on the 23rd of June when we received four CDs, and we signed the receipt on the 23rd of June, and we still don't have an English version nor do we have a witness who could add to the reliability of these documents. That is why we feel that this CD should not be admitted into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. We have no additional comments to make about the schedule that has been outlined. We do wish to make one additional point, though, in connection with the admissibility of the contested documents in general as it appears we're now at the end of the evidence being presented in relation to the admissibility of documents. The final two witnesses don't appear to be witnesses who have been called in relation to the documents. In our view, it is important that two gaps are identified for Your Honours to take into consideration when you render your decision in respect of documents. The first is, Your Honours, in our submission there are still a number of documents which have not been identified by any witnesses. The witnesses that have been called recently did identify some documents. For example, the witness today was able to identify seven documents, but there are many which the Prosecution has listed as documents where a witness could be called where that witness has not as yet been called. Now, we just wish to note that the list that was provided to Your Honours, as Your Honours ordered, of which witnesses could authenticate which documents, in that list there are a number of witnesses who -- who were not called. Of course we appreciate that not every single witness can be called, but we do note that not even a selection was made in order to seek to have witnesses to identify a number of the other documents that have not as yet been identified. Secondly, Your Honours, another gap which we wish to identify is that the evidence that the witnesses have given recently about the system that was in place for the preparation and issuing of orders applies from our assessment only at the level of the corps, the 3rd Corps and its command, and not at the brigade level or lower down, and certainly not between brigades either. In our submission, there's very little evidence in respect of the way in which orders were prepared and distributed at that level, and that's certainly a matter that applies specifically to our client, Mr. Kubura. The evidence that has been presented about the system that was in place, in our submission, may, of course, provide Your Honours with some assistance in determining the reliability of documents that have not been identified at either the 3rd Corps level or the brigade level, but in our submission, that does not change our fundamental point all along that it is necessary for a witness to identify a document and that it's not, in our view, the proper course to admit documents en bloc on the basis that a general system has been explained, but rather, it's necessary to look at each document one document by document and decide on the basis of the evidence that has been presented whether it does have sufficient indicia of reliability, the most important, in our view, being a witness who is able to identify that document. Those are our submissions which we would request Your Honours take into account in rendering your decision over the next week. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Dixon. We -- you have reminded us a number of times of what you have said, and rest assured that we understand fully your point. Perhaps Mr. Mundis has already replied to these points, but regarding more specifically to documents 585 and 586, the Defence tells us that they received four CDs on the 24th of June and that to this day they still haven't received translations of those documents. So clearly that when one closes one's case, there mustn't be any leftovers regarding lack of translations of certain documents. So, Mr. Mundis, what can you tell us, as it seems to me that it is quite certain that from now until ten -- ten or 15 days from now you will not be able to translate four CDs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's exactly right, Mr. President, and for that reason alone but perhaps other reasons as well, the Prosecution will withdraw Exhibits 585 and 586. We will not be seeking to rely on those registers. With respect to any of the other issues as raised by the Defence, again in the event the Chamber wishes to hear from any other witnesses, we will certainly assist in identifying and/or making any additional witnesses available to the Trial Chamber. The Prosecution submits that the witnesses and steps that we have taken pursuant to the Trial Chamber's oral order of 17 May, we have met those requests. I will inform the Chamber and the Defence as well that we believe there was one additional component beyond the documents which we're still receiving from the Translation Unit, and I can address that in a moment, but we will be filing later this afternoon a further spreadsheet indicating linkages or sequencing of documents, which was one of the specific tasks that we had been asked to do. So we have prepared -- again it will look like the other spreadsheets. There will be a column indicating how the documents, or some of the documents relate to each other in order -- in other words, an order to a unit and a response back from the unit, again demonstrating that documents were actually sent and received. And this was an exercise that was undertaken simply by looking at the documents themselves. We will be filing that later today. We will also be filing, either today or tomorrow, written submissions on the law and the armed conflict as the Chamber had inquired about last week, and I believe, Mr. President, other than the translations, we will be providing to the Chamber, again either later this afternoon or tomorrow, a spreadsheet indicating or a chart indicating which specific items on the legal officer's memo have been completed or when we expect to be able to complete that. With respect to the translations of the war logs, war diaries, we expect to have that back to us by close of business tomorrow in order to photocopy and collate that material and distribute it. We anticipate that that will be available to the Trial Chamber and the Defence sometime on Monday barring any unforeseen circumstances. And at that point, Mr. President, of course if there are any additional items that are missing, we will endeavour to provide those. As I indicated the week before last, due to the large volume and large number of documents it's certainly within the realm of possibility that individual sets would be missing a document here or there. If Your Honours or the Defence are missing particular documents, we're happy to make additional copies and make those available. And before we -- before we rise, Mr. President, I did have one final remaining issue to alert the Chamber about. Due to the fact that we had anticipated closing our case on the 1st of June and in light of the fact that it doesn't appear we will be sitting until the 12th of July, I would simply like to inform the Chamber that as of the end of next week, I will be away from the Tribunal and Ms. Benjamin will be here during the week of the 12th and onwards. I will, of course, be returning after the August recess, but I will not be here after the end of next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you won't be here at the end of next week, and we won't see you again until September; is that right? Or will you come at the end of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With any luck, Mr. President, a week from now I'll be on an aeroplane and I will return to The Hague on the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That, therefore, means that you will not be closing the Prosecution case but Madam Benjamin. Is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That is in fact correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Mundis, for telling us that. As you have said and I have already observed, we won't have hearings again until the 12th of July, the 12th of July. Should there be any problem regarding the 12th of July because of the availability or unavailability of the witness, you will let us know and tell us the exact date. As I have already said, the last date cannot be beyond the 23rd of July, because after that there's no further possibilities. And should there be any problems with the two witnesses, then the witnesses will have to be delayed until the beginning of September. There's no other way of dealing with it. Regarding this possibility of the witnesses not being available, has the Defence anything to tell us, but very briefly, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have no additional observations to make. We understand that in the week of the 12th the witnesses will be called, if possible, and the Defence will be ready to cross-examine those witnesses. Mr. President, the Defence would like to address a request to you, but if possible, we would like to do that in the absence of the accused in the courtroom, because it has to do with certain questions relating to the Defence and not to the rights of the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dixon, Mr. Ibrisimovic, regarding the schedule, do you have any observations to make or not regarding the schedule?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have no observations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, I would like to ask the security officers to be kind enough to accompany the accused out. We bid them goodbye, and we'll see them again in July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I give you the floor, as you have asked for it, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I will be very brief. First of all, I should like to confirm that I find myself in a very delicate position in addressing the Chamber on such a matter because it is a personal issue, because the Registrar has made certain points and allegations that I provided incomplete information to the Chamber, and my position is extremely delicate. I would have preferred my colleague to have raised this, but to be very brief, according the directives for the Defence counsel, it is the Chamber that determines the duration of the case. In this case, the procedures took longer than envisaged, and we would like the Chamber to take the necessary steps with the Registry so that the necessary adjustments be made so that we are remunerated according to the applicable norms for such cases. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
